title: Obstetric Cholestasis: Assessment, Fetal Surveillance and Delivery Planning

evidenceAudit.scope: Obstetric Cholestasis: Assessment, Fetal Surveillance and Delivery Planning
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: The full Wiley guideline text was not openly accessible; only RCOG summary material was opened.
Saudi maternity formulary and local delivery-timing policy require confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Pregnancy-related impairment of bile transport raises maternal bile acids. Bile acids cause pruritus and are associated with fetal risk at higher concentrations. Symptoms and biochemistry usually resolve after birth; persistence suggests another liver disorder.
keyMechanisms: Pregnancy-related impairment of bile transport raises maternal bile acids.
Bile acids cause pruritus and are associated with fetal risk at higher concentrations.
Symptoms and biochemistry usually resolve after birth; persistence suggests another liver disorder.

symptoms: Pruritus without a primary rash, often involving palms and soles and worse at night.
physicalSigns: Excoriations without a primary rash; jaundice is uncommon and needs broader liver assessment.
redFlags: Peak bile acids at least 100 micromol/L, jaundice, abnormal coagulation, reduced fetal movement or other obstetric concern.
precipitants: Previous intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, multiple pregnancy, liver disease or family history.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Alternative symptoms, imaging or serology abnormality.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Raised; risk stratified by peak concentration
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Repeat according to obstetric plan and use peak value for birth planning.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm and exclude alternatives
actions: Measure bile acids and liver profile; assess skin, medicines and alternative liver disease.

clinicalManagement.title: Risk-stratify and plan birth
actions: Base monitoring and planned-birth discussion on peak bile acids, gestation and other obstetric risks.
Discuss the higher fetal risk when peak bile acids are at least 100 micromol/L.

clinicalManagement.title: Postnatal confirmation
actions: Confirm symptom resolution and repeat liver tests/bile acids at the postnatal review.
Refer persistent abnormalities for hepatology assessment.

medicationPlan.note: Do not routinely prescribe ursodeoxycholic acid to prevent adverse perinatal outcomes. Symptom treatment, including any ursodeoxycholic-acid use, requires the maternity formulary and an individual discussion that it does not remove fetal risk or replace delivery planning.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Maternal pruritus with raised bile acids after exclusion of other causes; use the laboratory pregnancy range.
Peak bile acids at least 100 micromol/L (RCOG GTG 43).

teaching.scope: Obstetric Cholestasis: Assessment, Fetal Surveillance and Delivery Planning
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.
keyPoints: Peak bile acids at least 100 micromol/L, jaundice, abnormal coagulation, reduced fetal movement or other obstetric concern.

patientEducation: Explain itching management, fetal-movement safety net and the role of bile-acid results.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid unverified supplements; maintain normal pregnancy diet and hydration.
mdtReferrals: Obstetric/maternal-fetal medicine; hepatology for atypical or persistent disease.
dischargeCriteria: Not an emergency admission when clinically stable, but a documented maternity surveillance and birth plan is required.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Postnatal symptom and biochemical review, with recurrence counselling for future pregnancies.
